title: Change in Corneal Power Distribution in Orthokeratology: A Predictor for the Change in Axial Length

groups.description: single cohort fitted with Paragon CRT orthokeratology lenses, worn nightly for at least 8 consecutive hours; 67 completed cases of 76 enrolled; Fudan University Eye and ENT Hospital, Shanghai, China; mean age of the completed cases (Table 2)

series.notes: mean ± SD of Table 3 row 'AL (mm)' (baseline, 6 Month, 1 Year); right eyes only; the 67 completed cases of 76 enrolled (88%); axial length device not stated

exclusions.what: Table 3 row 'AL elongation (mm)' at 6 months and 1 year
exclusions.reason: change series of the same group; the absolute series is used when both are given

exclusions.what: Table 2 column 'Dropouts (n = 9)' and its baseline AL
exclusions.reason: baseline only, no follow-up axial length
baseline duplicated by Table 3 baseline, which is cited instead

exclusions.what: Table 3 1-month, 3-month and 9-month columns of the AL row
Table 3 SER, Ymax, Xmax and power exponent rows; P value column
exclusions.reason: not axial length; p-values are not admissible

notes: Prospective single-arm orthokeratology study, November 2019 to November 2020, Fudan University Eye and ENT Hospital, Shanghai, China; children aged 8-13 years.

76 enrolled; 9 who missed two or more visits were dropouts and were excluded from the analysis; 67 completed (88% of enrolled, at least 70%, protocol inclusion 5), with baseline data of completers and dropouts compared in Table 2.
Only right eyes were analysed (Statistical Analyses).
Axial length measured at baseline, 6 months and one year; the biometer is not named in the article.
Manifest refraction and corneal topography metrics are tabulated (Table 3) and are not extracted.
